g: (uncountable) A Japanese style of aquarium aquascaping that focuses on the simplistic yet harmonious placement of stones; (countable) an aquascape in this style.
(rare, uncountable) A similar style of stone placement but for gardens.
(mathematics) A deformation of the group algebra of a Coxeter group.
(mineralogy) A tetragonal-ditetragonal dipyramidal greenish black mineral containing iron, manganese, and oxygen.
A large, vaulted chamber with a monumental arched opening on one side.
Synonym of charr (“fish”) An ingredient in sushi and sashimi, sometimes referred to by its Japanese name when listed as an ingredient.
(New Zealand) An extended group of Maori kin groups or families, sharing common ancestry; a tribe. (An iwi is smaller than a waka and larger than a hapu.)
